question: Which offices may read the security events of an organization (authentication, authorization, data access, configuration and suspicious activity, with the source address and user agent), may a person or a process other than the platform record or resolve an event, and how is an event shown not to have been authored or edited by the person it concerns?
decision: System-authored append-only security events; no caller can create, overwrite or delete their own trail. Platform security under a scoped mandate may inspect high-detail logs. Tenant-designated security/privacy administrators see a redacted tenant-only view; ordinary org admins have no automatic access to secrets, IPs or cross-tenant investigations. Resolution creates a distinct linked immutable event, reviewed by someone other than the subject of investigation.
originalProposedDecision: Org admins and the platform security role read their org's events. Only the platform writes events; none may be edited or deleted; resolution is a separate appended record by a person who is not the event's subject.
independentApprovalScope: decision wording / platform baseline only; NOT independent security or operational testing
